messages:
Sam: Heads-up — noticed the runbook header refactor broke a bunch of in-page anchors we link to from incident playbooks. Example link now 404s: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall.md#page-ops. Anyone own runbooks-oncall?

Leila: I do — I refactored some headings yesterday. Sorry for the pain. Can you paste the exact failing link you saw?

Sam: Sure — the link in the incident doc points to `#page-ops`. Quick excerpt of the change that caused it:

```
- ## Page ops
+ ## Page operations
```

Ben: Yup that will change the anchor from `#page-ops` to `#page-operations`. Two quick options: restore the old header, or add an explicit HTML anchor under the new header so old links keep working. Prefer the anchor fallback for compatibility.

Leila: OK — I can do the anchor fallback plus update the incident links. Will open a tiny PR. @Ben can you review? ETA ~1h.

Ben: I can review after lunch. @Nora is this something Platformops needs backported to staging for the 09:30 oncall run?

Nora: Yes please — the oncall checklist references the old anchor. If the PR is small we'll cherry-pick it into staging. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #987 — preview available at https://staging.runbooks.redwood.preview/pr-987

Leila: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/987. Added a brief note in the description about why the anchor is kept as a compatibility shim and that we updated the source links (incident doc + handbook).

Sam: Thanks — I'll update the incident doc to point at the preview URL until the PR is merged. That avoids confusion for oncall.

Ben: Quick checklist before merge: (1) small unit test for table-of-contents generation not necessary, (2) sanity preview looks good, (3) approve + merge.

Leila: Will wait for your review, Ben. Thanks everyone!
